complexity_scope.guarantee: Deterministic pathwise upper bound for every admissible sequence.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: Displayed coefficients are explicit: 1/2 for D²√T and √T−1/2 for G²; no hidden dimension factor in this expression, and no projection runtime claim.
complexity_scope.oracle: Each round first makes a decision, then receives the cost function and computes its exact gradient at x_t; exact Euclidean projection is available.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Feasible per-round decisions; cumulative static regret against the best single fixed u∈F over the same horizon.
complexity_scope.regime: T≥1 integer, finite D,G≥0; asymptotic conclusion requires bounds uniform over the infinite sequence.
complexity_scope.resource: T-round full loop has T gradient computations and T exact projections; projection implementation cost separately charged, not bounded in this theorem. The final unused update may be omitted.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Selected deterministic Greedy Projection with η_t=t^(-1/2); not a lower bound for unrestricted algorithms.

issues.description: The source writes the gradient parameter as a maximum over infinitely many rounds, but standing assumption 5 guarantees only boundedness; the record retains its role as a finite uniform bound and does not claim that the maximum is attained. Every step of the Proof requires only this uniform bound.

evidence.statement_check: Theorem 1, all seven standing assumptions, Definitions 4/5, Algorithm 1, and the Proof were checked against the original-page images.

content.intended_use: Provides a finite-horizon static regret bound and an asymptotic average-regret upper guarantee for the selected Greedy Projection schedule.

proofs.locator: PDF page 4, both columns, Proof after Theorem 1 through its end before Section 2.2
map: Page 4 left column, opening paragraphs: set g_t=∇c_t(x_t). Replacing the costs with linear costs g_t·x leaves the Algorithm trajectory unchanged; convexity gives c_t(x_t)−c_t(u)≤⟨g_t,x_t−u⟩, so it suffices to bound the linearized regret.

Page 4 left column, y_{t+1} expansion and projection paragraph: expand ||y_{t+1}−u||₂² and use ||P_F(y)−u||₂²≤||y−u||₂² and ||g_t||₂≤G to obtain ⟨g_t,x_t−u⟩≤[||x_t−u||₂²−||x_{t+1}−u||₂²]/(2η_t)+η_tG²/2.

Page 4 right column, first display: use weighted telescoping for decreasing η_t; every feasible squared distance is ≤D², and dropping the nonpositive final term gives R_G(T)≤D²/(2η_T)+(G²/2)Σ_{t=1}^Tη_t.
Page 4 right column, final display and concluding sentence: η_t=1/√t, Σ_{t=1}^T1/√t≤1+∫_1^T s^(-1/2)ds=2√T−1; substitution gives Theorem 1.
proofs.omitted_details: This is a map of the source Proof actually read, not a locally reconstructed Proof or independent reproof; no new transfer claim is made. The Euclidean projection inequality used directly in the source is not separately proved in that Proof.
proofs.reading_coverage: Actually read the complete Proof in the page-labelled text and viewed both columns of formulas and the conclusion in the registered original-page JPEG of page 4; also viewed the complete statement, parameter definitions, and standing assumptions on page 3.

assumptions: For every positive integer t, c_t:F→R is convex and differentiable.
There exists finite G≥0 such that ||∇c_t(x)||₂≤G for all t≥1 and x∈F.
Each c_t has a computable gradient; exact P_F(y) can be computed for arbitrary y∈R^n.
Initialize at any x_1∈F; each round selects x_t before observing c_t, then updates x_{t+1}=P_F(x_t−η_t g_t) using exact g_t=∇c_t(x_t).
η_t=t^(-1/2); no D/G rescaling is used.
statement.conclusion: R_G(T)≤(D²/2)√T+(√T−1/2)G². For an infinite sequence satisfying the uniform bound over all rounds, limsup_{T→∞}R_G(T)/T≤0. This does not claim that average regret is necessarily nonnegative or that its limit necessarily equals zero.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Euclidean R^n; known F⊆R^n. D=diam₂(F)=max_{x,y∈F}||x−y||₂. G denotes a finite uniform gradient norm bound for all t≥1,x∈F. P_F(y)=argmin_{x∈F}||x−y||₂. R_G(T)=Σ_{t=1}^T c_t(x_t)−min_{u∈F}Σ_{t=1}^T c_t(u). The source uses ||F|| and ||∇c|| for D and the gradient bound, respectively.
statement.parameter_domains: n is a positive integer; t,T∈{1,2,...}; D,G are finite nonnegative real numbers, allowing D=0 or G=0; η_t>0.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every F satisfying the assumptions, every infinite cost sequence satisfying the uniform gradient bound, every x_1∈F, and every positive integer T, the following bound holds. The Algorithm is deterministic and the bound is a pathwise guarantee for each sequence; no distributional assumptions or relations between successive costs are required.
